topic_ko: 창꼬치 실험 — 실패 뒤 사라진 장벽 앞에서도 멈추듯, 실패의 두려움이 성장을 막는다

passage: Scientists once put a barracuda, a violent fish, into a tank with some mackerel.
As expected, the hungry barracuda attacked the small fish.
Then the scientists placed a glass panel between them.
The barracuda kept hitting the glass, but it could not reach the mackerel.
After bumping its nose many times, it finally gave up.
Even after the glass was removed, it stopped where the barrier used to be.
Many people act the same way after they fail.
Their fear of failure stops them from growing, even though failure can lead to success.
choices: how scientists catch large fish in the sea
why barracudas are dangerous to people
the best way to build a large aquarium
how mackerel escape from bigger fish
how the fear of failure can stop our growth
theme.explanation_ko: 유리판에 막혀 포기한 창꼬치처럼 사람도 실패 후 시도를 멈추고, 그 두려움이 성장을 막는다는 내용이므로 ⑤가 주제이다.
theme.distractor_ko: ① 물고기를 잡는 방법이 아니다. ② 사람에게 위험하다는 내용은 없다. ③ 수조 만드는 법이 아니다. ④ 고등어가 도망치는 이야기가 아니다.

passage: A barracuda is a large fish known for its violent behavior.
In an experiment, it tried again and again to attack some mackerel behind a glass panel.
Each time, it only bumped its nose and failed.
At last, it quit trying.
Later, the glass was taken away, but the barracuda still would not swim past that spot.
It believed the barrier was still there.
Like the barracuda, people often stop trying after they fail.
But failure is often a step toward success, so we should not let fear limit us.
choices: 실패에 대한 두려움 때문에 시도를 멈추면 성장할 수 없다.
과학 실험에 동물을 이용해서는 안 된다.
위험한 일은 처음부터 시도하지 않는 것이 좋다.
포식성 물고기는 먹이를 쉽게 포기하지 않는다.
gist.explanation_ko: 실패는 성공으로 가는 한 걸음이니 두려움이 우리를 제한하게 두지 말라는 마지막 문장이 요지이므로 ①이 알맞다.
gist.distractor_ko: ② 실험의 옳고 그름은 다루지 않는다. ③ 오히려 계속 시도해야 한다. ④ 창꼬치는 장벽이 사라져도 멈췄다. ⑤ 창꼬치는 결국 포기했다.

passage: Scientists once put a barracuda, a violent fish, into a tank with some mackerel.
As expected, the hungry barracuda attacked the small fish.
Then the scientists placed a glass panel between them.
The barracuda kept hitting the glass, but it could not reach the mackerel.
After bumping its nose many times, it finally gave up.
Even after the glass was removed, it stopped where the barrier used to be.
Many people act the same way after they fail.
Their fear of failure stops them from growing, even though failure can lead to success.
choices: How to Keep Fish in a Tank
title.explanation_ko: 실제 유리판은 사라졌지만 창꼬치(와 사람)의 마음속에 남은 두려움이 벽 역할을 하므로 ② ‘두려움이라는 보이지 않는 벽’이 알맞다.
title.distractor_ko: ① 물고기 기르는 법이 아니다. ③ 창꼬치를 칭송하는 글이 아니다. ④ 고등어의 속도는 나오지 않는다. ⑤ 유리판은 깨진 것이 아니라 치워졌다.

passage: Scientists put a glass panel between a hungry barracuda and some mackerel.
The barracuda attacked again and again, but it only bumped its nose.
Finally, it quit trying.
When the glass was removed, the barracuda still stopped at the same spot.
Many of us also carry an invisible glass panel in our minds after we fail.
It is not real, but it keeps us from trying again.
implication.underlined: an invisible glass panel in our minds
choices: a window that helps us see clearly
a good memory of past success
a fear that comes from past failure
a rule made by our teachers
a real wall that blocks our way
implication.explanation_ko: 실패한 뒤 마음속에 남아 다시 시도하지 못하게 막는 것이므로 ③ ‘과거의 실패에서 생긴 두려움’을 뜻한다.
implication.distractor_ko: ① 잘 보이게 돕는 창이 아니다. ② 성공의 기억이 아니라 실패의 기억이다. ④ 선생님의 규칙이 아니다. ⑤ 본문은 ‘실제가 아니다(It is not real)’라고 했다.

passage: Scientists carried out a simple experiment on a barracuda.
They put it into a big aquarium with some small fish called mackerel.
Not noticing the glass panel, the barracuda tried to attack the mackerel.
After bumping its nose many times, it finally quit to try.
Later, the barrier was removed.
grammar.explanation_ko: quit 은 동명사를 목적어로 취하므로 quit to try 는 quit trying ‘시도하기를 그만두다’가 되어야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ① carry out ‘수행하다’의 과거형. ② ‘~라고 불리는’ 과거분사가 fish 를 꾸민다. ③ 분사구문의 부정은 not 을 분사 앞에. ⑤ 장벽이 ‘제거된’ 것이므로 수동태.

passage: A barracuda is a large predatory fish known for its violent behavior.
Scientists placed a glass panel between it and the mackerel.
The barracuda tried to attack the mackerel in vain.
Even after the barrier was removed, it stopped at the same place.
This shows that the fear of failure can increase our growth.
vocab.explanation_ko: 실패의 두려움 때문에 다시 시도하지 못하므로 두려움은 성장을 ‘늘리는(increase)’ 것이 아니라 ‘제한한다(limit)’.
vocab.distractor_ko: ① 다른 물고기를 잡아먹는 ‘포식성의’. ② 유리판을 ‘놓았다’. ③ 공격은 ‘헛수고’였다. ④ 장벽이 ‘제거되었다’.

passage: Scientists put a glass panel between a barracuda and some mackerel.
The barracuda attacked many times but only bumped its nose.
In the end, it stopped trying.
When the glass was taken away, it still swam only to where the glass had been.
It did not try again because it ______________________.
People can be like this barracuda after a failure.
choices: believed the glass was still there
did not like the taste of mackerel
wanted to play with the mackerel
was too tired to swim any farther
blank.explanation_ko: 유리가 있던 곳까지만 헤엄쳐 가서 멈춘 것은 유리판이 ‘아직 그곳에 있다고 믿었기’ 때문이다(원문 It believed that the glass panel was still there!).
blank.distractor_ko: ② 배고픔이 사라졌다는 말은 없다. ③ 고등어의 맛 이야기는 없다. ④ 함께 놀고 싶었던 것이 아니다. ⑤ 지쳐서가 아니라 장벽이 있다고 믿었기 때문이다.

irrelevant.intro: Scientists once did a simple experiment with a barracuda.
sentences: They put it into a big tank with some small fish called mackerel.
Barracudas can grow very long and swim at high speed.
Then they placed a glass panel between the barracuda and the mackerel.
The barracuda attacked again and again until it finally quit trying.
Even after the glass was removed, it never crossed that spot again.
irrelevant.explanation_ko: ②는 창꼬치의 몸길이와 속도에 관한 일반 정보로, 실험의 과정과 결과를 다루는 흐름과 무관하다.
irrelevant.distractor_ko: ① 실험 준비, ③ 유리판 설치, ④ 반복된 공격과 포기, ⑤ 유리판을 치운 뒤의 결과 — 모두 실험의 흐름에 맞다.

order.given: Some time ago, scientists put a barracuda, a large and violent fish, into a big aquarium with some small mackerel.

blocks.A: Not noticing the glass, the barracuda tried to attack again and again. After bumping its nose many times, it finally quit trying.
blocks.B: As they expected, the hungry barracuda attacked the mackerel. But then the scientists placed a glass panel between them.
blocks.C: Later, the barrier was removed, but the barracuda still stopped where the glass had been. Like the barracuda, many people stop trying after they fail.

order.explanation_ko: 실험 준비(주어진 글) → 공격과 유리판 설치(B) → 유리를 모르고 공격하다 포기(A) → 유리를 치운 뒤의 결과와 교훈(C) 순이다.
order.distractor_ko: (A)의 the glass 는 (B)에서 처음 나오는 a glass panel 을 받고, (C)의 the barrier was removed 는 포기(A) 이후의 일이다.

insert.insert_sentence: Interestingly, it still stopped at the place where the barrier had been.

passage_marked.text: Scientists placed a glass panel between a barracuda and some mackerel.
The barracuda attacked again and again but only bumped its nose.
Then the scientists removed the glass panel.
It believed that the glass was still there!

insert.explanation_ko: 장벽이 ‘있었던(had been)’ 곳에서 멈춘 것은 유리판을 치운 뒤의 일이고, 그 이유가 마지막 문장(아직 있다고 믿었다)이므로 ④에 들어간다.
insert.distractor_ko: ①②③ 은 유리판이 아직 있을 때라 had been 이 맞지 않는다. ⑤ 이유(믿었다)가 결과보다 먼저 나오게 된다.

passage: A barracuda is a large fish known for its violent behavior.
In an experiment, it tried again and again to attack some mackerel behind a glass panel.
Each time, it only bumped its nose and failed.
At last, it quit trying.
Later, the glass was taken away, but the barracuda still would not swim past that spot.
It believed the barrier was still there.
Like the barracuda, people often stop trying after they fail.
But failure is often a step toward success, so we should not let fear limit us.
summary.summary_template: After failing many times, the barracuda stopped __(A)__ even when the barrier was gone, just as people let the __(B)__ of failure limit their growth.
summary.explanation_ko: 창꼬치는 장벽이 사라져도 시도(trying)를 멈췄고, 사람도 실패의 두려움(fear)이 성장을 제한하게 둔다.
summary.distractor_ko: ① 먹기를 멈춘 것이 아니다. ② 기쁨(joy)이 아니다. ③ 성공(success)이 아니라 실패의 두려움이다. ④ 숨은 것이 아니다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: 전치사 After 뒤에는 동명사 bumping, quit 의 목적어도 동명사 trying.
writing.answer: After bumping its nose repeatedly, the barracuda finally quit trying.
writing.ko_prompt: 코를 반복해서 부딪친 후, 창꼬치는 마침내 시도하는 것을 그만두었다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 우리말을 영작하시오.
conditions: 부정 분사구문 Not noticing 으로 시작할 것
writing.explanation_ko: Not noticing ~ = As(Because) it didn’t notice ~. tried to attack ‘공격하려고 애썼다’, in vain ‘헛되이’.
writing.answer: Not noticing there was a glass panel, the barracuda tried to attack the mackerel in vain again and again.
writing.ko_prompt: 유리판이 있다는 것을 알아차리지 못하고, 창꼬치는 계속해서 고등어를 공격하려 했지만 헛수고였다.

writing.question: 본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
writing.context: This fear limits our growth even ___________ failure is often a step toward success.
writing.explanation_ko: even though + 주어 + 동사 ‘비록 ~이지만, ~인데도’. 본문 11번 문장이다.

writing.question: 다음 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.explanation_ko: would 는 과거의 반복적 습관 ‘~하곤 했다’, where the barrier had been 은 ‘장벽이 있었던 곳’(과거완료).
writing.en_prompt: Interestingly, thereafter, the barracuda would swim only to where the barrier had been and stop.
writing.answer: 흥미롭게도, 그 후로 창꼬치는 장벽이 있었던 곳까지만 헤엄쳐 가서 멈추곤 했다.

writing.question: 본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말을 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Like the barracuda, many people stop __(A)__ after experiencing failure, and this fear __(B)__ their growth.
writing.explanation_ko: 본문 10번 문장의 stop trying, 11번 문장의 This fear limits our growth 에서 찾는다.

writing.question: 다음 조건에 맞게 이 글의 주제문을 영어로 쓰시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 이 글의 주제를 한 문장으로 쓰시오.
conditions: failure 와 fear 를 반드시 포함할 것
writing.answer: We should not let the fear of failure stop us from trying, because failure is a step toward success.
writing.explanation_ko: 실패의 두려움이 시도를 막는다는 문제와 실패가 성공으로 가는 한 걸음이라는 교훈을 함께 담는다.
